title: Slowing the label around 1980 and the CD reissues
summary: He slowed Strata-East around 1980, focused on writing in the 80s, reissued favorites on CD around 1989, and never considered stopping performing.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: just went quiet with it you know. And anyway the digital age was coming and I just, you know during the 80s I just concentrated solely on writing music, taking bands wherever. And around ’89 with the digital format now getting ready to really shoot out there, I re- tooled and re-issued on CD just those LPs that I liked that we still were doing. The LP merchandising never stopped because the Japanese, you know, they were gung ho on this from the jump. And the Brits, you know. So overseas things still went on as usual. I just wasn’t going to be strapped down to going into an office situation you know.

Did you ever feel the need to take a break not only from your label but from actually performing and composing? Did the business of finding gigs, etcetera — I can see you’re shaking your head so that, yeah —

No. That would have been impossible, not only because of how I am but because I am my grandmother and my mother. So you finish what you start. So it was never, that was not going to happen. So it was never a thought of doing that, it’s always been full out, full stop. ‘Til now. I think maybe that’s what keeps me going you know, is I still, as I began, I just wanted to belong you know? I just wanted to belong to this great art form, and so I was given a chance to do that by Jackie McLean.
